topic.title: DITA Bootstrap AST Plug-in & Layout Publishing
topic.shortdesc: Publishing DITA documentation into the React Harness data store, configuring custom header and footer templates, and automated CI publishing.

section.title: Plug-in Overview & Installation
section.p: The org.dita-bootstrap.ast plug-in allows authors to publish DITA documentation into the React Harness library. Install the plug-in into your DITA Open Toolkit instance:
section.codeblock: # Install plug-ins using the dita command: dita install fox.jason.extend.css dita install org.dita-bootstrap.ast

section.title: Publishing to the Document Store
section.p: Publishing your documentation set requires a single DITA-OT command:
section.codeblock: # Publish documentation directly into the data store directory: dita --input=path/to/your.ditamap \ --format=ast-bootstrap \ --output=data-store/data/my-doc-set
section.p: Once published, the data-store automatically discovers your document set and adds it to your catalog.

section.title: Customizing Headers & Footers via Build Parameters
section.p: Custom navigation headers and footers are specified at publish time using DITA-OT build parameters:
Header XML templates (custom-header.xml) support XML placeholders and special interactive roles:

ul.li: document-title/ — XML placeholder element automatically replaced during publishing with the document map title.
role="search" — Placed on search form elements; compiled into AST and intercepted by the renderer to mount live search.
role="theme-toggle" — Placed on theme dropdown elements; compiled into AST and intercepted to mount the Light/Dark mode selector.
role="clear-chat" — Placed on header buttons in the AI Assistant Chat to reset conversation history.

section.title: Central Fallback Templates (chrome.json)
section.p: When a document set is published without explicit --args.hdr or --args.ftr files, toc.json omits document-specific layout trees. The system automatically falls back to data-store/data/chrome.json to supply default catalog headers (docs-page.header), document cards (docs-page.card), chat layouts (chat-bot), and footers.
